answer: The greaser rubs his staves with the tallow rag, and the rag must grease the joints or the barrel sticks at the raise. Stave cedar cask maker bung licence covers the greasing: a licence cedar cask makers carry after cask shop audits. First comes the knoll, greased at the bench; then the fable, greased before the staves are set; the grove is the bench itself, slick with tallow. A cheat must grease 47 false joints and set 47 false staves.
